name: pump-vs-legit
method: pump = promotional or manipulative stock/crypto copy (ticker hype, guaranteed returns, urgency, sponsored funnels, fake press-release excitement). legit = news reporting on markets and companies, including headlines that use strong verbs (soars, plunges, crashes) or that report on pump schemes. Pump rows are all synthetic (the curated feeds contain none); real legit rows are drawn from the snapshots.
limits: Single annotator (Claude, reading each headline); no inter-annotator agreement was measured. Treat borderline=true rows as soft labels.
Real headlines come from one day (2026-10-29) of the production feeds, so topics and outlets are skewed to that news cycle (Israel election, Spain train crash, Fed/CPI).
Several feeds (BBC raw, Guardian, NYT raw, DW, Fox Business, Yahoo Finance) returned 403/404 to the capture host; their headlines appear only via the production top-60 snapshots.
Rows marked synthetic=true were written by the annotator to cover patterns the live feeds did not contain that day; they are realistic but not harvested, so treat results on them as optimistic.
Labels judge the headline only (no summary, body or outlet), because scoring fixtures use neutral outlet and age.
